figures.title: Queensland — drink driving deaths and serious injuries
wording: accounts for more than a fifth of all lives lost on Queensland roads
figures.source: Queensland StreetSmarts / Department of Transport and Main Roads (2026)

figures.title: Queensland — drug driving deaths and serious injuries
figures.source: Queensland StreetSmarts / Department of Transport and Main Roads (2026)

figures.title: Queensland — self-reported driving over the limit, including the next day
wording: 11% of Queenslanders admit to driving when they are over the alcohol limit, while 21% admit to driving the next day when they may be over the limit.
figures.source: Cited on Queensland StreetSmarts, “Drink driving: Get the facts,” from Footprints Market Research, Driver Attitudes & Behaviour State-wide Research, January 2026.
figures.note: This is a Queensland self-report survey cited by a state road-safety site, not a crash or fatality figure, and not a national official statistic.

figures.title: New South Wales — drink driving in fatal crashes
wording: Drink driving is a factor in about one in every seven crashes in NSW where someone loses their life.
figures.note: The official page does not name a year or range for this figure.

figures.title: Victoria — drivers and riders killed with BAC greater than .05
wording: in the last five years, around one in five drivers and riders who lost their lives had a BAC greater than .05.
figures.note: The official page says “the last five years” but does not name the years.

figures.title: Victoria — drugs detected in killed drivers and riders
wording: In the five years from 2019-2023, 40% of all drivers and riders killed who were tested had drugs in their system.

figures.title: Victoria — stimulants and cannabis in 2023 fatalities
wording: 17% of driver and rider fatalities in 2023 had stimulants in their system and 11% had cannabis in their system.

figures.title: Victoria — crash risk at a BAC of .05
wording: At a BAC of .05, your risk of being involved in a road crash is about double compared with a BAC of zero.
figures.period: Not dated on the page (presented as a current official statement).
figures.note: This is a risk comparison, not a safe limit or a target. Alcohol affects people differently. Being under the limit is not the same as being safe to drive.
